subject: math
title: Counting to 200: Skip Counting by 2s, 5s, 10s, 20s, 25s and 50s
seo_title: Grade 2 Counting to 200 Math Worksheets: Skip Counting, Free with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Count to 200, including by 20s, 25s, and 50s, using a variety of tools and strategies
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on counting to 200 for the Ontario curriculum: count on and back by 1s and 10s, skip count by 2s, 5s, 20s, 25s and 50s with mitts, nickels and quarters, and fill in number lines and number charts. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Skip counting means jumping by the same number each time.
key_sub: Count by 25s like quarters: 25, 50, 75, 100, not 90. Past 100, 100 and 5 more is 105, not 1005.
body_html:
Skip counting: jump by the same number

When you skip count, you jump by the same amount each time. In Grade 2 you count to 200 by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, 20s, 25s and 50s.

Count byExampleLook for
2s36, 38, 40, 42Skip every other number
5s85, 90, 95, 100The ones digit is 0 or 5
10s23, 33, 43, 53Only the tens digit changes
20s100, 120, 140, 160Five 20s make 100
25s25, 50, 75, 100The numbers end in 25, 50, 75, 00
50s50, 100, 150, 200Two 50s make 100

Count by 10s from any number

You can start at any number. When you count by 10s, the ones digit stays the same.

On a number chart, the number just below is 10 more. The number just right is 1 more.

Count by 25s with quarters

A quarter is 25¢. Count quarters by 25s. 4 quarters make 100¢, or $1. That is a loonie.

Count by 25s

Count by 25s: 100, 125, 150, ☐

Each number is 25 more. 150 + 25 = 175.

Answer: 175

Going past 100

After 100, the numbers start again with a 1 in front: 101, 102, 103 … 110, 120. 100 and 5 more is 105. It has 3 digits, not 4.

Count byPast 100
1s98, 99, 100, 101, 102
5s90, 95, 100, 105, 110
10s80, 90, 100, 110, 120
1s197, 198, 199, 200

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting 25, 50, 75, 90Keep jumping by 25: 75 + 25 = 100
Writing 1005 after 100 when counting by 5s100 and 5 more is 105
Writing 1010 after 109109 + 1 = 110
Changing the ones digit when counting by 10s: 23, 33, 44Keep the ones digit: 23, 33, 43
Counting pairs, not things (8 pairs = 8 boots)Count by 2s: 8 pairs = 16 boots
Counting the start as a jumpCount only the numbers you land on

faq.q: What counting is in the Grade 2 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Expectation B1.4 asks Grade 2 students to count to 200, including by 20s, 25s and 50s, using tools like number lines, number charts and coins. They also count on and back by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s from any number.

faq.q: Why do Grade 2 students count by 25s?
faq.a: Counting by 25s is counting quarters. Four quarters make $1 (a loonie) and eight quarters make $2 (a toonie), so it builds money sense too.

faq.q: Why does my child write 1005 after 100 when counting by 5s?
faq.a: They write “100” and then “5”, the way the number sounds. Show that 100 and 5 more is 105, which has only 3 digits, on a number chart or a number line.

faq.q: How can I practise counting to 200 at home?
faq.a: Count real things in groups: pairs of mitts by 2s, nickels by 5s, dimes by 10s and quarters by 25s. Ask your child to count on and back from a number like 96 or 185, past 100 and up to 200.

sets.title: Count on and back by 1s and 10s

items.q: Count on: 46, 47, 48, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 more. 48 + 1 = 49.

items.q: Count by 10s: 30, 40, 50, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 50 + 10 = 60. 51 is only 1 more.

items.q: The marks go up by 1 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count on by 1s from 115: 116, 117, 118.

items.q: What number comes just before 160?
items.e: Count back 1 from 160: 159. 161 comes just after 160.

items.q: Count by 10s: 23, 33, 43, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. The ones digit stays 3. Only the tens digit goes up. 43 + 10 = 53.

items.q: Count back: 142, 141, 140, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 less. 140 − 1 = 139. Just before 140 is 139, not 130.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 90, 80, 70, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 less. 70 − 10 = 60. 69 is only 1 less.

items.q: This is part of a number chart. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 74. 74 + 10 = 84.

items.q: Start at 58. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +10. Count by 10s from 58: 68, 78, 88. You land on 88.

items.q: Count on: 107, 108, 109, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 109 + 1 = 110. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. Write 110, not 1010.

items.q: Count by 10s: 80, 90, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 100 + 10 = 110. 1 hundred and 1 ten is 110, not 1010.

items.q: The marks go up by 1 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count on by 1s from 96: 97, 98, 99, 100. After 99 comes 100, not 910.

items.q: Count on: 117, 118, 119, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 119 + 1 = 120. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. So 11 tens become 12 tens.

items.q: Count back: 103, 102, 101, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 less. 101 − 1 = 100. Do not skip 100. 99 comes after it.

items.q: Count by 10s: 76, 86, 96, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 96 + 10 = 106. 9 tens and 1 more ten make 1 hundred. The ones digit stays 6.

items.q: Count by 10s: 145, 155, 165, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up. 165 + 10 = 175.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 132, 122, 112, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 less. The ones digit stays 2. 112 − 10 = 102. Keep the 0 in the tens place.

items.q: Start at 175. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is back 10. Count back by 10s: 165, 155, 145. You land on 145.

items.q: This is part of a number chart. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 188. 188 + 10 = 198. Or count on 1 from 197.

items.q: What number comes just after 199?
items.e: 199 + 1 = 200. 9 ones and 1 more make a ten. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a hundred. So 1 hundred becomes 2 hundreds.

items.q: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Count by 2s. How many mitts are there?
items.e: A pair is 2 mitts. Count by 2s, one pair at a time: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 mitts.

items.q: Count by 5s: 15, 20, 25, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 25 + 5 = 30.

items.q: A nickel is 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 5s, one nickel at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 30¢.

items.q: Count by 2s: 31, 33, 35, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 35 + 2 = 37. 36 is counting by 1s.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Each group has 5 marks. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. There are 35 marks.

items.q: Count back by 5s: 70, 65, 60, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less. 60 − 5 = 55. 59 is counting back by 1s.

items.q: Start at 46. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +2. Count by 2s from 46: 48, 50, 52, 54. You land on 54.

items.q: Count by 2s. How many mitts are there?
items.e: A pair is 2 mitts. Count by 2s, one pair at a time: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. There are 18 mitts.

items.q: Count by 5s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting by 5s from 0, every number ends in 0 or 5: 75, 80, 85. 82, 58 and 93 do not.

items.q: Count back by 2s: 150, 148, 146, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 less. 146 − 2 = 144.

items.q: A nickel is 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 5s, one nickel at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60. That is 60¢.

items.q: Count by 5s: 135, 140, ☐, 150. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 5 more than 140. 140 + 5 = 145. Then 145 + 5 = 150.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Count the groups by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. Then count on 3 by 1s: 21, 22, 23. There are 23 marks.

items.q: Count by 2s: 96, 98, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 100 + 2 = 102. 1 hundred and 2 ones is 102, not 1002.

items.q: Count by 5s: 90, 95, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 100 + 5 = 105. 1 hundred and 5 ones is 105. Do not write 1005.

items.q: Start at 120. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +5. Count by 5s from 120: 125, 130, 135, 140. You land on 140.

items.q: Count back by 5s: 110, 105, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less. 100 − 5 = 95. 99 is only 1 less.

items.q: Count by 2s: 186, 188, ☐, 192. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 2 more than 188. 188 + 2 = 190. Then 190 + 2 = 192.

items.q: Count by 5s: 185, 190, 195, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 195 + 5 = 200. 5 ones and 5 more ones make a ten. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a hundred. So 195 becomes 200.

items.q: Count by 20s: 20, 40, 60, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 20 more. 60 + 20 = 80. 70 is counting by 10s.

items.q: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more. 75 + 25 = 100. After 75 do not switch to 10s (90).

items.q: A quarter is 25¢. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 25s, one quarter at a time: 25, 50, 75. That is 75¢.

items.q: Count by 20s: 10, 30, 50, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 20 more. The tens digit goes up by 2. 50 + 20 = 70.

items.q: Count by 20s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting by 20s from 0: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160. 150, 170 and 90 are not in the list.

items.q: A quarter is 25¢. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. That is 100¢. 100¢ is $1, the same as a loonie.

items.q: Start at 40. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +20. Count by 20s from 40: 60, 80, 100. You land on 100.

items.q: Count by 25s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting by 25s from 0: 25, 50, 75, 100. The numbers end in 25, 50, 75 or 00.

items.q: Count by 20s: 100, 120, 140, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 20 more. 140 + 20 = 160. 150 is counting by 10s.

items.q: How many quarters make $1 (100¢)?
items.e: Count by 25s until you reach 100: 25, 50, 75, 100. That is 4 quarters.

items.q: Count by 20s: 60, 80, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 100 + 20 = 120. 1 hundred and 2 tens is 120, not 1020.

items.q: Count by 25s: 50, 75, ☐, 125. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 25 more than 75. 75 + 25 = 100. Then 100 + 25 = 125.

items.q: Count by 20s: 120, ☐, 160, 180. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 20 more than 120. 120 + 20 = 140. Then 140 + 20 = 160.

items.q: A quarter is 25¢. How much money is this?
Which list counts by 25s?
items.e: Each number must be 25 more: 25, 50, 75, 100. In 25, 50, 75, 90 the last jump is only 15.

items.q: Count back by 20s: 200, 180, 160, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 20 less. 160 − 20 = 140.

items.q: Count by 25s: 100, 125, 150, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more. 150 + 25 = 175. 200 is counting by 50s.

items.q: Start at 50. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +25. Count by 25s from 50: 75, 100, 125, 150. You land on 150.

items.q: Count back by 25s: 200, 175, 150, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 less. 150 − 25 = 125.

items.q: How many quarters make $2 (200¢), the same as a toonie?

sets.title: Count by 50s and find the rule

items.q: Count by 50s: 0, 50, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more. 100 + 50 = 150. 1 hundred and 5 tens is 150, not 1050.

items.q: Start at 0. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +50. Count by 50s from 0: 50, 100, 150. You land on 150.

items.q: Count by 50s: 50, 100, 150, ☐. What comes next?
How many 50s make 100?
items.e: Count by 50s: 50, 100. That is 2 fifties.

items.q: Count by 50s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting by 50s from 0: 50, 100, 150, 200. 125 is counting by 25s.

items.q: Count back by 50s: 200, 150, 100, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 less. 100 − 50 = 50. 90 is counting back by 10s.

items.q: How many 50s make 200?
items.e: Count by 50s: 50, 100, 150, 200. That is 4 fifties.

items.q: Count by 50s: 10, 60, 110, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more. 110 + 50 = 160. The ones digit stays 0.

items.q: Start at 70. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +50. Count by 50s from 70: 120, 170. You land on 170.

items.q: What is the rule? 35, 85, 135, 185
items.e: Each number is 50 more: 35 + 50 = 85. The rule is count by 50s.

items.q: Count by 50s: 25, 75, 125, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more. 125 + 50 = 175.

items.q: Which list counts by 50s?
items.e: Each number must be 50 more: 20, 70, 120, 170. 20, 25, 30, 35 counts by 5s.

items.q: Count by 50s: 30, 80, ☐, 180. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 50 more than 80. 80 + 50 = 130. Then 130 + 50 = 180.

items.q: What is the rule? 100, 125, 150, 175
items.e: Each number is 25 more: 100 + 25 = 125. The rule is count by 25s.

items.q: Start at 200. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is back 50. Count back by 50s: 150, 100, 50. You land on 50.

items.q: Count back by 50s: 190, 140, 90, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 less. 90 − 50 = 40.

items.q: What is the rule? 40, 60, 80, 100
items.e: Each number is 20 more: 40 + 20 = 60. The rule is count by 20s.

items.q: What number is 50 more than 135?
items.e: Count on 50 from 135. 135 + 50 = 185. Only the tens digit changes: 3 tens + 5 tens = 8 tens.

items.q: What is the rule? 160, 150, 140, 130
items.e: The numbers get smaller by 10 each time. The rule is count back by 10s.

items.q: You count by 50s from 0. Your friend counts by 25s from 0. Which number do you both say?

sets.title: Number lines, charts and word problems

items.q: The marks go up by 2 each time. What number goes at the ?
The marks go up by 5 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count by 5s from 80: 85, 90, 95.

items.q: The marks go up by 10 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count by 10s from 60: 70, 80, 90, 100. After 90 comes 100, not 910.

items.q: This is part of a number chart. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 125. 125 + 10 = 135.

items.q: This is part of a number chart. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 175. 175 + 10 = 185.

items.q: This is part of a number chart. What number goes at the ?
items.e: The number below the ? is 155. The row above is 10 less. 155 − 10 = 145.

items.q: The marks go up by 20 each time. What number goes at the ?
The marks go up by 25 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count by 25s from 0: 25, 50, 75, 100. Not 90: keep jumping by 25.

items.q: The marks go up by 50 each time. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count by 50s from 0: 50, 100, 150. Write 150, not 1050.

items.q: Nathan sees 8 pairs of winter boots by the classroom door. How many boots are there?
items.e: A pair is 2 boots. Count by 2s 8 times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. There are 16 boots.

items.q: Leah sees Canada geese fly by in groups of 5. She counts 8 groups. How many geese are there?
items.e: Count by 5s 8 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. There are 40 geese.

items.q: Ethan has 9 nickels. A nickel is 5¢. How much money does he have?
Maya reads 20 pages each night. How many pages does she read in 5 nights?
items.e: Count by 20s 5 times: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. That is 100 pages.

items.q: Liam has 150 stickers. He gives away 10 stickers each day. How many stickers are left after 3 days?
items.e: Start at 150 and count back by 10s 3 times: 140, 130, 120. He has 120 stickers left.

items.q: A sugar bush has 120 bottles of maple syrup. Each hour, the workers fill 10 more. How many bottles are there after 4 hours?
items.e: Start at 120 and count by 10s 4 times: 130, 140, 150, 160. There are 160 bottles.

items.q: Hana has 5 quarters. A quarter is 25¢. How much money does she have?
A box holds 25 hockey pucks. The rink has 6 boxes. How many pucks are there?
items.e: Count by 25s 6 times: 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150. There are 150 pucks.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Olivia runs 4 laps around the gym. Each lap is 50 m. How far does she run?
items.e: Count by 50s 4 times: 50, 100, 150, 200. She runs 200 m.

items.q: Chloe has 5 boxes of 20 crayons and 3 more crayons. How many crayons does she have?
items.e: Count the boxes by 20s: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Then count on 3 by 1s: 101, 102, 103. She has 103 crayons.

items.q: Arjun puts 1 quarter in his piggy bank each day. How many days until he has $2 (200¢)?
items.e: Count by 25s to 200: 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200. That is 8 quarters, so 8 days.
